symbols.name: cpu_work
symbols.doc: CPU-bound arithmetic — the profiler's favourite patient.

symbols.name: cpu_burn_mixed
symbols.doc:
Calls cpu_work in rounds and mixes in small sleeps — so a CPU profile
    shows both burning time (cpu_work) and waiting (time.sleep), not just one.

symbols.name: quick_task
symbols.doc:
One small unit of work for the pipeline (sleeps a beat so the
    concurrency timeline shows overlapping threads).

symbols.name: pipeline
symbols.doc:
Run `tasks` units across `workers` threads and record every span.

    Returns a list of {thread, task, start_ms, end_ms} measured with
    time.monotonic() — the raw material of the concurrency timeline chart.

symbols.name: allocate_blocks
symbols.doc:
Allocate `blocks` chunks of `size` bytes while tracemalloc watches —
    the memory profile's raw material (top sites + totals).

symbols.name: racing_counter
symbols.doc:
A REAL data race: threads do read-modify-write on one integer with no
    lock. CPython's GIL makes each single bytecode atomic, but the three-step
    read-add-write is not — updates get lost whenever a thread switch lands
    between the read and the write.

    widen=False: the natural window. On CPython 3.12 the switch check lands
    on the loop backedge, so short runs may lose nothing — that

symbols.name: cyclomatic
symbols.doc:
CC = 1 + decision points (if/elif, for, while, except, bool-ops,
    ternary, comprehension-ifs, assert, match cases).

symbols.name: collect_repair_loop
symbols.doc:
Really execute three fail→fix→recheck cycles in a temp copy and time them.
    Each bug gets its own module + its own test, so one cycle's failure is
    caused by that bug alone (clean detect → repair → recheck).

symbols.name: parse_faulthandler_stacks
symbols.doc: Group faulthandler dump frames per thread header.

symbols.name: run
symbols.doc: Run a command for real; keep the real exit code and output.

symbols.name: make_sandbox
symbols.doc: Copy bankapp into a temp dir, git init, commit the baseline.

symbols.name: apply_candidate
symbols.doc:
Copy the candidate feature in and commit it — the real candidate
    change the walkthrough talks about.

symbols.name: git_history_rows
symbols.doc:
One pass over the repo's real history: per top-level part, commits,
    distinct authors (hashed at source), last-touch age.

symbols.name: github_fetch
symbols.doc:
Real read-only calls to the GitHub API for the repo this sample
    ships in. If the operator supplied a key (env CIE_GITHUB_TOKEN), it is
    used in the Authorization header ONLY — the key itself is never written
    to any artifact, and only its health is recorded.

symbols.name: measure_replay
symbols.doc: US-076 — really trace bankapp's own good_auth('alice').

symbols.name: measure_duplicate
symbols.doc: US-081 — really deliver one order twice with no idempotency key.

symbols.name: measure_slow_trace
symbols.doc: US-082 — one slow request, split into compute vs waiting, really.

symbols.name: measure_speed_pair
symbols.doc: US-083 (prove faster) + US-084 (show slowdown), both really.

symbols.name: measure_sandbox_compare
symbols.doc:
US-101 — really run both pricing variants on the same basket.
    The basket is chosen so per-line rounding really differs from
    round-at-the-end: eight lines where half-cents accumulate.

symbols.name: measure_journeys
symbols.doc: US-115 — really walk the three journeys through the candidate.

symbols.name: measure_build
symbols.doc:
US-117 — really compile every bankapp module, and prove a failure
    shows up: one control target is deliberately broken and really fails.

symbols.name: measure_fix_recheck
symbols.doc: US-121 — really run the failing test first, then the fix, then the rerun.

symbols.name: export_patch
symbols.doc: US-122 — really export the candidate as a patch file.

symbols.name: measure_apply
symbols.doc:
US-123 — really apply the patch twice: once clean, once against a
    diverged copy, so the conflict is a real one.

symbols.name: measure_consequences
symbols.doc: US-116 — the real bill of consequences: what the candidate adds.

symbols.name: record_plan_story
symbols.doc: US-104 — the intake moment.

symbols.name: record_clarifications
symbols.doc: US-105 — only what matters, each with why it matters.

symbols.name: record_brief
symbols.doc: US-108 — the approval-worthy brief, real content.

symbols.name: record_revision
symbols.doc: US-110 — the scope really changed: 500 → 1000 + monthly reset.

symbols.name: record_wizard
symbols.doc: US-112 — the six stages, checkpointed at real moments.

symbols.name: record_draft_pr
symbols.doc: US-124 — prepared, honestly not published.

symbols.name: record_approvals
symbols.doc: US-129 — the self-approval was really denied by the rule, in record.

symbols.name: record_checklist
symbols.doc: US-130 — the checklist assumes real failure; every number is real.

symbols.name: record_editor_focus
symbols.doc: US-132 — what focus sharing gives away, and what it never does.

symbols.name: can_transfer
symbols.doc: must refuse transfers above the spending limit

symbols.name: transfer
symbols.doc: must refuse transfers above the spending limit; must reject bad input

symbols.name: replay_authorize
symbols.doc:
Trace bankapp's own good_auth("alice") line by line.

    Returns the raw event list (function, line, event, locals-at-return).
    This is a REAL execution of the real auth.py code in this project.

symbols.name: _external_call
symbols.doc: Stands in for a payment-processor API call: pure waiting, no CPU.

symbols.name: _db_query
symbols.doc: Stands in for a database round-trip: pure waiting, no CPU.

symbols.name: _password_check
symbols.doc: Real KDF work: pbkdf2 with 120k iterations — genuine CPU burn.

symbols.name: slow_request
symbols.doc:
One slow request, honestly composed of the three cost kinds:
    real CPU work (pbkdf2), waiting on an outside service (sleep), and
    waiting on the data store (sleep). cProfile separates them because
    sleep shows up as time spent inside time.sleep, not inside our code.

symbols.name: duplicate_delivery
symbols.doc:
Deliver the same order twice (what a retrying queue honestly does),
    with no idempotency key — then count what the ledger actually holds.

symbols.name: _locked_pipeline
symbols.doc:
A deliberately serialized pipeline: one global lock around each task.
    Used as the 'after the change' run in the slowdown story (US-084).

symbols.name: _free_pipeline
symbols.doc: The unmodified pipeline shape (same work, no global lock).

symbols.name: bench
symbols.doc:
Run the same workload several times; keep EVERY run in the count,
    including failures. Median is computed over all completed runs.

symbols.name: price_variant_a
symbols.doc: Round once at the end (what most ledgers do).

symbols.name: price_variant_b
symbols.doc: Round after every line (what some carts do).

symbols.name: sandbox_compare
symbols.doc:
Run both pricing variants on the same basket, in-process but
    logically isolated (same inputs, independent calls). Failures stay
    in the count — an empty basket is part of the contract, not noise.

symbols.name: can_transfer
symbols.doc: must refuse transfers above the spending limit

symbols.name: transfer
symbols.doc: must refuse transfers above the spending limit; must reject bad input

symbols.name: journey
symbols.doc: Walk one real journey through the candidate: 'ok', 'denied' or 'error'.
